answer:
Alexander the Great founded Alexandria, Egypt — the city where Euclid, considered the "father" and founder of geometry, lived and worked during the Hellenistic period (circa 300 BC).

Alexander the Great established Alexandria around 331 BC as one of his many city foundations during his Egyptian campaign following his conquest of the Persian Empire. The city became a major center of learning and science in the ancient world, home to the famous Library of Alexandria and the Mouseion, where Euclid taught at the Great Library and wrote his seminal work *Elements* that formalized geometric principles still studied today.
